items.title: Act II/III density: decision 047 removed the blocker, now spend it — re-author Act II/III wave composition for more, lighter units at constant wave leak_cost, then re-sweep anchors 09-24
items.note:
PREMISE RE-MEASURED 2026-07-28; the original note was wrong on all three counts.
1. The roster is not the constraint: ~0.52 dps/MW against shielded/armoured vs ~1.0 against plain is a 2x penalty, not an absence. The proposed mid-cost anti-armour emplacement would not have helped.
2. Throughput is not the constraint: 2x damage on every weapon AND +60% capacity (3.2x throughput) still reaches only 1/11 winning builds at weight 1.50 on anchor-20.
3. 'Does not grade clean at any life count' was false — anchor-20 at weight 1.50 grades clean at 72 lives. Never tested: sweep.py defaults to weights [0.85, 1.0, 1.15] and the anchor's current life count.

ROOT CAUSE, now fixed by decision 047: density and leak-tension were the same axis, because a leak cost one life whether it was a 22 hp mote or a 520 hp Column. leak_cost = max(1, round(hp/130)) makes trading one Column for four ~130 hp units tension-neutral.

REMAINING WORK, mechanical and not blocked on the owner: re-author Act II and III wave composition to field more, lighter units in place of the bricks, holding each wave's total leak_cost roughly where it is, then re-sweep anchors 09-24. Judge the result on leak budget (lives / total leak_cost), not on raw lives — Act I sits at 8.7%, Act II 18.0%, Act III 30.4%.

items.title: Hollow lit cones are laterally off-axis from their dark cones, so the emissive collapses at yaw 315. cone() rotates each primitive about its own origin, so two cones sharing rot=(11,-8,0) but sitting at different z have parallel axes offset by ~0.045 world units (~4px): the lit cone pokes out on the +x+y side and hides behind the dark cone from the opposite camera. Measured glow coverage hollow_shard 0.0061 at y315 vs 0.024-0.036 elsewhere; hollow_echo 0.0089 vs 0.042-0.068. Currently latent because anchor_view.gd only ever draws y045 (see the sibling item). Fix is to put the lit cone on the dark cone's rotated axis, or to build both from one origin, and it applies to the whole Hollow set at once rather than shard alone

anchor_view.gd hardcodes yaw 45 for every drawable (drawables(), lines 495 and 508), so 156 of the 208 atlas cells are never drawn. The pipeline renders, masks, packs and imports four yaws per asset and the manifest exposes all four, but nothing picks one from unit heading or tower target. Consequence beyond the wasted 3/4 of the atlas: yaw-only art defects are invisible in game, which is how the Hollow yaw-315 emissive collapse survived unnoticed. Either drive yaw from movement direction, or drop to a single yaw and stop rendering the other three

check_banned_terms() rglobs the whole repo and only exempts docs/NOMENCLATURE.md by exact path, so a git worktree under .claude/worktrees/ carrying its own copy of the bible failed the gate with six false hits. Fixed by skipping .claude alongside .venv, addons and .godot. Kept as a record of the second-order trap it exposed: the backlog itself is scanned, so an item that quotes the terms it is about turns the gate red — the item must describe the hits, never repeat them

Board camera: pan and zoom. Pan on middle-drag plus lf_* keys and edge-scroll, NOT left-drag — left click arms builds and selects emplacements, so drag-to-pan turns every slipped click into a camera move. The board cursor should carry the camera with it, which gives keyboard and gamepad panning without a second system. Zoom transforms the BOARD LAYER ONLY: the HUD ladder and palette were solved for WCAG AA at a known size (045/046) and scaling them with the board silently undoes it. Zoom out is cheap; zoom in past 1.0 softens sprites, which are a fixed 256px atlas at one orthographic scale, so either raise the render base or clamp. Value is inspection on a busy board, not navigation — a 17x13 grid already fits — so it must never be required to play. Needs a --camera x,y,zoom verification hook or every --shot/--a11y report becomes camera-state dependent
items.note: Landed: CAM-01 (pan/zoom/edge-scroll/cursor-follow) and CAM-03 (--camera verification hook). scripts/anchor_view.gd, scripts/main.gd, scripts/backdrop.gd, tools/godot/setup_input.gd, tools/shot.py, tools/validate/a11y.py.

items.title: standard_policies() cannot express a mixed board: every Policy is a total preference order and _try_build fills every free slot greedily from the top, so a graded build is all-of-one-thing. 'Three pulse turrets in front of an ion lance' is not in the search space, which makes claims like 'the escort brings the cheap emplacements back' unfalsifiable by the harness that is supposed to test them. Needs capped-core policies (cap the expensive tower at N, fill the rest cheap)

PRESSURE_FLOOR in sim/run.py is a dead check: peak load ratio is >=100% of capacity on all 24 anchors x 3 difficulties, and still >=75% everywhere with the greedy-overdraw policy excluded, so 'the player is pressed against capacity' can never fail. Either measure pressure on winning builds only, or raise the floor until it discriminates

anchor_sim._step's splash loop tests 'u == target' but Godot 4.7 compares Dictionary by value (probed: two dicts with equal contents are ==, and Array.find matches by value), while sim/engine.py tests 'u is target'. Two units of the same kind with equal hp and equal dist therefore drop out of splash damage in GDScript and take it in Python. Latent only because same-kind units spawn on different ticks so their dist differs — a wave table that spawns two identical units on the same tick turns it into a parity failure. Found while deciding where facing state could live (LF-050); the fix is an identity-safe test on the GDScript side, e.g. comparing by index
items.note: fixed by comparing target by index; Godot Dictionary == is a value comparison, probed

items.title: Running the editor import (godot --headless --path . --import) rewrote scripts/menu.gd from tab indentation to four-space indentation, a 442-line no-op diff that has to be reverted by hand before committing. The gate's rendered checks read display state from the player's save. window_mode, resolution and ui_scale live in user://progress.json, which is outside the repo, so game renders / menu renders / accessibility measured whatever the last person left set — the same tree reported coverage 0.56 and 0.34 on two machines, and the a11y analyser samples its background colours out of those frames. Fixed by leading every rendered check with --display-defaults; kept as the record of why, and because any future verification hook that persists state (the LF-052 board camera especially) has the same hole

The game renders gate check took 2,187,910 ms (36 min) on one run and then PASSED, against 2,493 ms on another run of the same tree the same day. CAUSE, observed by the owner: the three rendered checks launch a REAL Godot window (GL Compatibility reads back nothing headlessly), and macOS throttles a window it considers occluded — cover it, background it, or just keep working in front of it and the frame loop stalls, so main.gd's 'await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw' never resolves. The run does not fail, it waits until the window is visible again and then passes, which is why the gate stayed green. Two mitigations are in: tools/check.py bounds every subprocess (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT 300s, PARITY_TIMEOUT 1800s) and reaps grandchildren on timeout, so a stall is now a red run naming the check; and --no-window skips the three windowed checks so the gate is usable while someone is at the machine. Neither is a fix. A real fix makes the capture independent of the compositor presenting frames — candidates: RenderingServer.force_draw() instead of awaiting frame_post_draw, or rendering the shot through a SubViewport. Both need probing against Godot 4.7.1 on this machine, and the occlusion stall has to be reproduced on purpose first (cover the window during a --shot run) or there is no way to tell a fix from a coincidence
items.note: Closed by decision 052: on this WSL2 machine, tools/toolpaths.godot() prefers the native Linux Godot build and tools/toolpaths.godot_argv(want_window=False) runs it under an Xvfb virtual framebuffer via xvfb-run. Verified: tools/shot.py anchor-06 --frames 600 reproduces coverage=0.6153 distinct=112 err=0 with zero windows shown, matching the visible-window baseline exactly. tools/check.py's game renders/menu renders/accessibility and tools/test_parity.py all go through the same path now. A machine with no native Linux Godot build or no xvfb-run still falls back to the old visible-window path, so the trap remains real there.

items.title: The subagent model pin has two holes the agent models gate check cannot see. (1) Built-in agents — Explore, Plan, general-purpose — have no .claude/agents/*.md frontmatter to carry model: sonnet, so they inherit the parent (Opus) unless the model is passed at each call site. Nothing enforces that; it is discipline, and discipline is what failed the first time. (2) The SessionEnd reap hook does not fire when the CLI is killed outright rather than exiting cleanly, so the wrap-skill step is the only real belt and it depends on someone running the wrap. Both are cheap to narrow: a wrapper or documented default for built-in agent calls, and a launchd/login reap or a stale-process check at session start (the start skill now runs reap.py, which covers the common case one session later rather than immediately). Filed because the whole point of decision 051 was replacing remembered rules with mechanical ones, and these two are still remembered rules

board_props.gd's platform edge/ring geometry currently renders as a large opaque shape that covers most of the tile diamond on anchor-06 and anchor-01, leaving only a small unclipped sliver near the board's top corner visible. Observed via tools/shot.py screenshots taken during the combat-FX pass (this session): anchor-06 frame 1800 captured twice about ten minutes apart with identical STATE lines but very different board coverage (first capture showed the full diamond, second showed the cutoff). items.note: Misdiagnosed under time pressure. Root cause was a parse error in this session's own combat_fx.gd/fx_additive.gd: several 'var x := view.to_screen(...)' / 'fx.tile_radius_screen(...)' lines failed GDScript's static type inference because view/fx are held as bare Node2D, which failed the whole script's load. CombatFx.bind() (called from AnchorView.boot() before _centre() at the time) then threw on the missing method, aborting boot() before _origin was computed -- so the board collapsed to a corner and backdrop.gd's horizon glow showed through what looked like an oversized board_props.gd shape. board_props.gd and backdrop.gd were never at fault. Fixed by giving those locals explicit types and by making boot() call combat_fx.bind() last, guarded with has_method(), after _centre().

Wire sim.unit_leaked -> _fire('first-leak') and add a lives-fraction threshold -> _fire('low-lives') in anchor_view.gd.

recovery-taken (draft screen, between anchors) has no natural home in the per-anchor dialog architecture -- draft.gd has no DialogView instance at all (only main.tscn/anchor_view.gd wires one up), and dialog files are keyed to a specific anchor id that check_dialog() cross-references. The two recovery-taken lines are authored in anchor-01.json as a stopgap and will only ever play there. Proper fix needs either (a) a small reaction display built directly on draft.tscn/draft.gd reading from its own data source, or (b) a real campaign-scoped dialog concept (new anchor-pattern value, validator update) rather than borrowing one anchor's file. Also wire scripts/draft.gd's _on_take() (or whatever call site replaces it) to actually surface the line -- right now nothing on that screen fires dialog_trigger.

mask_glow.py re-saves every glow PNG in the manifest on every run, not only the ones a render actually changed. PIL's save() does not reproduce identical bytes for identical pixel content across invocations, so re-running it after a partial re-render (e.g. --only one asset) touches every other sprite's LFS blob with a pixel-identical but byte-different file — confirmed via git-lfs smudge + numpy compare on hollow_column_y045_glow.png: max abs pixel diff 0, but sha256 differs from HEAD. Harmless to the game, but it turns every glow-pass re-render into a full-repo LFS diff and makes 'what actually changed' unreadable from git status. Fix: skip re-saving a glow PNG whose computed output already matches what is on disk, or track per-file content hashes the way pack_atlas.py already does for the atlas page.

The --autoplay smoke policy (_autobuild_step in anchor_view.gd) fills every free slot with the single highest-priority-affordable tower in Content.unlocked_at() order, so a board never shows a mix of weapon classes -- confirmed while trying to screenshot a mortar/flak burst for the combat-FX pass: anchor-09, anchor-13, anchor-16 and anchor-21 all built out one tower type (arc-node or anchor-damper) and never touched flak-array or mortar-emplacement even many waves in. This is the same root cause LF-053 already names for grading. A '--build <tower-id> <slot-x>,<slot-y>' CLI hook in main.gd would let --shot verify a specific weapon's FX/behaviour on demand without fighting the autobuild policy.

tools/shot.py's --extra nargs='*' cannot pass any flag-shaped token (--scroll 3, --paused, --select 1) -- argparse classifies any argv item starting with '-' as option-like and refuses to fold it into nargs='*', so 'unrecognized arguments' aborts before Godot ever launches. Confirmed with a standalone argparse repro, not anchor-specific. The tool's own docstring/epilog example ('--extra --select 1 --pick pulse-turret') has apparently never actually been run. Workaround used this session: invoke the native Linux Godot binary directly under xvfb-run with the same argv tools/toolpaths.godot_argv() builds, bypassing shot.py's argparse. Fix is probably nargs=argparse.REMAINDER (consumes everything after --extra verbatim, order-preserved) rather than nargs='*'.

scripts/anchor_view.gd's boot() hands sim.setup() Content.towers/Content.enemies/Content.anchor(anchor_id) directly -- scripts/loadout.gd (Loadout.towers()/enemies()/anchor()) is never called anywhere in the codebase. Confirmed by grep. Six of the nine recovery effects (tower_draw_mult, bounty_mult, starting_funds_add, tower_damage_mult, range_mult, and by extension anything Loadout would apply) are therefore completely inert regardless of what the player owns -- only the three effects read directly at their call sites (sell_refund_add, surge_charge_mult, veterancy_mult) do anything, and this session wired those three in (Threshold Surge charge rate, veterancy rank thresholds). Fix is almost certainly three lines in anchor_view.gd's boot(): sim.setup(Loadout.anchor(anchor), Loadout.towers(Content.towers), Loadout.enemies(Content.enemies), difficulty). Left unfixed this session because it is a between-anchor progression system gap discovered while wiring the abilities/pacing/targeting/veterancy task, not part of that task, and scripts/loadout.gd is out of scope to touch.

Rebuilding .godot/ blanks the level for anyone playing out of the same tree. The owner plays from D:\dev\Latticefall while agents edit /mnt/d/dev/Latticefall — the same directory. An agent moved .godot aside to force a cold import and the running game lost every imported texture: menu still drew (plain UI), level came up blank. Diagnosed as a code regression for a full pass before the real cause surfaced. Also: an import performed by the Linux Godot build is not sufficient for the Windows editor, which re-imports on open — that was the step that actually restored it. Mitigation is documented in CLAUDE.md; a mechanical version would be a guard in tools/ that refuses to touch .godot while a Godot process is live, or a shot.py flag that imports in place rather than cold

THEATRE SCALE 01. Board camera: pan, zoom, edge-scroll and cursor-follow. At 48x48 and above the board exceeds the viewport several times over, so this stops being a convenience and becomes how the game is read. Scoping is in docs/STATE.md under LF-052, with two corrections from this session: AnchorView.position is now taken by the screen-shake trauma system so a camera must compose with it rather than own the transform, and Backdrop sizes itself to the raw viewport independently of the board so scaling the parent would tear it
items.why: Nothing larger than one screen is playable without it
items.note: Landed: CAM-01. ZOOM_MIN is derived per-board from tile extent vs. the strip (decision 056), floored at 0.05 so the projection cannot degenerate. Verified on anchor-24 (2112px board) at 100% and 200% interface scale.

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 02. Cull and cache board tile drawing. _draw_board() is O(w*h) every frame with no culling and no caching; at 64x64 that is 4096 tile draws per frame before a single unit moves. Needs viewport culling plus a cached static layer, since ground, path and slot tiles never change during a level
items.why: First thing that falls over as the board grows

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 03. Spatial hash for target acquisition. _step() is O(emplacements x units) with an inner O(units) splash loop; at 60 emplacements and 400 units that is 24000 distance checks per tick at 30 Hz. Needs grid bucketing or per-tower target caching with a re-acquire interval. Must be mirrored in sim/engine.py and must not change WHICH unit is selected, or parity breaks
items.why: Sim cost is the hard ceiling on unit count

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 04. Minimap with threat and power overlay. Once the board exceeds the screen the player cannot see where the trouble is; the minimap becomes the primary readout for lane pressure and for which region of the grid is browned out
items.why: The player cannot defend what they cannot see

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 05. Large-board authoring tooling. Hand-authoring a 64x64 multi-lane anchor is not viable and the generator has to exist before the content does. Extends tools/densify.py's preview-first method: generate layout plus lane set plus slot placement, preview it, then grade it
items.why: The generator must precede the content

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 06. Multi-lane paths and multiple spawn points. The structural blocker: anchor JSON carries a single path array, and anchor_sim.gd and sim/engine.py are both built around one point_at(), one path_length and a leak test of dist >= path_length. Supporting 2-5 simultaneous lanes and up to 4 spawn points is what makes a front line exist at all. Both rule implementations must move together or parity is lost
items.why: Without it there is no flank, only a longer queue

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 07. Raise the unit budget to 250-400 alive. Depends on the spatial hash. Also needs the drawables() rebuild reviewed: it allocates and sorts an Array of Dictionaries and is called several times per frame across the view, the glow layer and both FX layers
items.why: Mass is what makes ground feel contested rather than queued

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 08. Unit roles and formations: screens, breakers, siege. Four hundred units walking single file is not an army. Needs units that advance together, shield each other, and behave differently when the lane ahead is blocked
items.why: Behaviour is what turns a crowd into an attack

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 09. Relay nodes: player-built power generation placed on the board, feeding a radius around themselves. Turns capacity from a number handed down by the brief into ground the player takes and defends. Rule change, so it must be mirrored in sim/engine.py
items.why: Makes supply something you hold rather than something you are given

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 10. The pulse: an enemy attack that suppresses rather than damages, taking every emplacement inside a radius offline for a few seconds. The counter is depth and redundancy rather than more damage. Note _covered_by() is a radius test over placed emplacements with no notion of a timed effect ON an emplacement, so this needs a new effect shape in both rule implementations
items.why: The enemy needs an answer to a dense line that is not just more hit points

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 11. Per-node power grid, so supply is regional rather than one global capacity_mw. Losing a flank should cost the guns on that flank. Large rules change; check first whether it can be expressed as data plus an existing effect type before adding a new rule shape
items.why: One global number cannot survive a board this size

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 12. Siege Battery: multi-tube salvo with a long reload, arcing over the whole board, drawing almost nothing between salvos and enormously during one. The first weapon that spikes the bus rather than loading it, which is a genuinely new shape for the power economy
items.why: A new shape of draw, not just a bigger number

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 13. Cutting Lance: a sustained beam held on one target with damage ramping the longer it holds, so switching targets wastes it. Needs a persistent-beam FX class; the current beam class is a 0.18s snap, not a held state
items.why: A gun that punishes target switching

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 14. Spine Driver: charges off spare bus capacity and fires a line that pierces everything in it. The only weapon that rewards staying UNDER capacity, which inverts the usual pressure and is the reason it is worth building
items.why: Inverts the power pressure the whole game is built on

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 15. Raise the sprite atlas from 256px to 512px cells and add pages. Four times the pixels per cell; orthographic scale is derived from cell width so the projection stays exact. Measure atlas memory and full-library render time on this machine before committing, since the library will also be growing
items.why: Fidelity, and the pipeline is scripted so it is machine time not artist time

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 16. Turret animation: traverse, recoil and reload frames. A turret that visibly turns and recoils sells mass better than any particle effect. Frames are cheap in the atlas and the pivot is already measured, but this multiplies cell count so it interacts with the atlas page budget
items.why: Sells weight better than particles do

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 17. Three environment sets with weather and a hazard each, one per act. Each act already owns an antagonist, a power tier and a mechanic; giving it a place with its own light and ground hazard is what makes the campaign feel like it travels
items.why: Each act should be somewhere, not just a palette

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 18. Dynamic score and battlefield mix responding to wave intensity, so pressure is audible before it is visible. The audio director already ducks music on brownout; this extends that idea to the whole fight
items.why: Intensity should be heard before it is read

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 19. A grading policy that can press a button. THE LARGEST HOLE IN THE PROJECT. sim/engine.py never uses speed, call-wave, the kill chain, an ability, targeting priority or veterancy, so every one of the 24 anchor grades describes a player who uses none of them. That was an acceptable floor when sell() was the only unmodelled verb; it is not acceptable now that a third of the game is unmodelled, and scaling the board multiplies the gap rather than closing it
items.why: Every balance number currently describes a player who never presses anything

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 20. Capped-core policies so a graded build can be mixed. Every Policy is a total preference order and _try_build fills every free slot greedily from the top, so a graded build is all-of-one-thing and claims like this escort makes the cheap gun matter are untestable. Prerequisite for grading a 60-emplacement board meaningfully. Supersedes LF-053
items.why: A 60-slot board graded as all-of-one-thing tells you nothing

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 21. Re-grade the whole campaign at theatre scale. Density targets, leak budgets and the capacity ladder all move with board size, lane count and unit budget; the wave-density gate check will need its act comparison rebased
items.why: Every balance figure moves when the board does

items.title: THEATRE SCALE 22. Performance budget in the gate. A frame-time regression should be a red run rather than a feeling. Needs a fixed-fps timing harness with a per-anchor budget so scaling work cannot silently cost 20ms a frame
items.why: Otherwise performance regresses invisibly

items.title: An emplacement with nothing in range re-scans every unit on every tick, forever. anchor_sim.gd _step(): when target.is_empty() it does p.erase(aim); continue WITHOUT resetting cooldown, which has already gone <= 0 — so the next tick scans all U units again. Same in sim/engine.py. MEASURED: a board whose guns cover a currently empty lane costs 2.19x at 8 towers/32 units rising to 2.87x at 100/800 versus the same board with targets in range. This is exactly the shape a big multi-lane board produces, since most guns are idle most of the time. Fix must be mirrored in both engines and must not change WHICH unit is selected
items.why: 2.9x sim cost for guns that are doing nothing

items.title: _covered_by() is called per unit per tick from the movement loop and iterates EVERY placed emplacement, testing eff.get(type) != effect inside the loop — so it costs O(towers) per unit even when no emplacement on the board has that effect at all. MEASURED: this is the unconditional 0.248-0.275 microseconds per tower-unit pair floor that persists even when only ~4 percent of towers are off cooldown. At 60 towers and 400 units that is 24000 wasted iterations per tick, 30 times a second. Fix is to filter placed by effect type once per tick; about ten lines in each rule file, mirrored
items.why: Pure waste in the hottest loop, paid even when the effect is unused

items.title: fx_additive _draw_hit_flashes() is quadratic in unit count: it scans the live hit list for every unit, and the hit list grows with the number of units being shot. MEASURED at 32x32: 0.31ms at 150 units, 0.96 at 300, 3.67 at 600, 7.67 at 900 — roughly U^1.9, and 29 percent of all draw cost at 900 units. Fix is to key hits by tile bucket rather than scanning. Presentation only, no parity exposure
items.why: The only quadratic term in the renderer

items.title: drawables() is rebuilt and re-sorted FOUR times per frame — anchor_view.gd:1152 and :1154 (shadow and sprite passes), glow_layer.gd:36, fx_additive.gd:209. Each call allocates an Array of one Dictionary per emplacement and per unit, computes depth, yaw and screen position, then sort_custom with a GDScript lambda. MEASURED at about 3.2 microseconds per entity per call, so 12.8 per entity per frame. Building it once and sharing it is 1.46x on its own and 2.47x combined with tile-list caching at 64x64 with 60 emplacements and 400 units. Presentation only
items.why: Four identical rebuilds and sorts per frame

items.title: tools/blender/render.py calibrate() cannot converge at 384 or 1024 px cells. It corrects ORTHO_SCALE from the WIDTH ratio only, so a one pixel height shortfall never resolves — reproduced deterministically: tile 192x95 against expected 192x96, and 512x255 against 512x256. 256 and 512 happen to work by luck. This blocks raising the render base, so it is a prerequisite for any atlas resolution increase. Also note pack_atlas.py has its own hardcoded CELL = 256 that is not read from the manifest, so two constants must move in lockstep
items.why: Blocks raising sprite fidelity at all

items.title: validate_data.py computes board saturation from base draw_mw only and never looks at upgrade.draw_mw, so an emplacement's upgraded draw is invisible to the saturation guard. Latent today; it starts to matter as soon as there are spectacle weapons with steep upgrade draws, which is exactly what the theatre-scale plan adds
items.why: The guard that protects the power decision does not see upgraded draw

items.title: THEATRE SCALE. Sprite legibility at zoom-out is a design problem, not a camera feature. MEASURED: fitting a 64x64 board needs zoom 0.234x at 100 percent interface scale and 0.117x at 200 percent, which renders a 256px sprite at 30-60px on screen — likely below the threshold for telling one enemy type from another. So a big board plus a fixed 256px atlas is a legibility wall. Options are bigger tiles (raising Iso.TILE_W/TILE_H, a whole-game layout change touching every screen-space calculation, the measured pivot and the a11y baselines), a zoom floor with a minimap doing the wide read, or silhouette-first art authored to survive 30px. This needs a human decision before the camera work is finished
items.why: The camera cannot fix what the art cannot show

items.title: PARITY BLIND SPOT: the gate never tests the build the owner plays. tools/test_parity.py goes through toolpaths.godot_argv(), and toolpaths.godot() prefers the native Linux build, so all 864 parity runs compare CPython against LINUX Godot. The owner plays the WINDOWS build. MEASURED across 100000 float64 samples on three runtimes: sqrt, fmod, +-*/, floor, round and manual hypot are byte-identical on all three, but Windows Godot (MSVC UCRT) diverges from CPython and Linux Godot (glibc) on atan2 0.084 percent, sin 0.133, cos 0.120, pow 0.130, log 0.031, exp 0.069 and tan 4.32 percent of samples. The rules currently use none of those ops so parity holds today BY ACCIDENT, not by design. Two fixes, both cheap: run test_parity.py against the Windows build at least once per release, and add a gate check that greps anchor_sim.gd and engine.py for the unsafe op set
items.why: The build that ships is never compared against the reference

items.title: DECISION 030 IS PARTLY WRONG AND IT IS BLOCKING WORK. It says square roots are unsafe in the rules. MEASURED: IEEE-754 requires sqrt to be correctly rounded, both runtimes issue SQRTSD, and sqrt matched 100000 of 100000 samples across CPython, Linux Godot and Windows Godot. The actual culprit in decision 030 was Vector2.distance_to, a FLOAT32 helper: for 2 million points placed exactly on an integer radius, float32 and float64 disagree on the <= r test 10.2 percent of the time. So the rule to carry forward is float64 and never Vector2, NOT never sqrt. This matters because it unblocks off-grid geometry: continuous positions with sqrt-normalised directions ran 4000 ticks x 64 units bit-identical on all three runtimes. Supersede decision 030 with an entry that names the safe op set (+ - * / sqrt fmod floor min max comparisons) and the banned set (atan2 sin cos tan pow log exp, and anything through Vector2)
items.why: A wrong rule is blocking a feature it was never about

items.title: Free placement removes the denominator from the board saturation invariant. validate_data.py bounds capacity_mw against len(slots) x max_draw, and CLAUDE.md plus STATE.md both record this as a trap that already bit once: anchor-24 reached 103 percent of what would run every slot at maximum draw and the power decision the whole game is about had stopped existing on five levels. With no slots, board saturation is unbounded and the check has nothing to divide by. It must be re-derived from something else before free placement ships: a hard emplacement cap, buildable area divided by footprint area, or funds. This is the single biggest non-obvious cost of free placement and it attacks the core hook directly
items.why: Free placement silently deletes the guard protecting the power economy

items.title: YAW_HYSTERESIS_DEG is 12.0 in iso.gd, which is LARGER than half a bucket at 16 yaws (11.25 degrees). If the yaw count is raised to 16 without changing it, an emplacement facing locks permanently and never re-buckets. Decision 049 measured that band empirically at 4 yaws (116 changes with 40 reversals became 59 changes with 3 reversals); the measurement has to be redone at the new bucket width. Also note three places independently encode the yaw count: render.py YAWS, iso.gd's 90 * roundi(deg/90) bucketing, and iso.gd's 45.0 + hysteresis test
items.why: Raising yaw count silently freezes every turret facing

items.title: tools/shot.py cannot take a menu screenshot and its comment used to claim it could. shot.py unconditionally forwards --anchor and --shot, and menu.gd's _boot_from_cli() tests argv.has('--anchor') or argv.has('--shot') BEFORE it looks at --shot-menu, so --extra --shot-menu is silently dropped and the run screenshots the game instead (confirmed: SHOT/FRAME emitted, MENUFRAME never). The gate's 'menu renders' check reaches it by other means, so this is only a hole in the everyday tool. Fix is a shot.py --menu mode that skips forwarding --anchor/--shot, or a menu.gd precedence change. Found while verifying PRC-09.

CAM-08's real acceptance number was never taken: the issue verifies with tools/shot.py --extra --profile 600, and --profile is CAM-06's deliverable which does not exist in scripts/main.gd yet. The bucketing was proved by a standalone microbenchmark (scripts/test/hit_bucket.gd: per-call cost flat at 2.2-2.9us across 150/300/600/900 units, against a linear reference that climbs 9.3 to 58.1us) plus a 910-query differential test with 0 mismatches. That is the right shape but a different instrument from LF-100's in-engine 7.67ms at 900 units. Re-run the issue's stated command once --profile lands and record the real in-frame number against the 1.0ms target.

The 'whole-frame SHA-256 must match' verification pattern used across several camera and FX issues cannot work on any frame containing combat. combat_fx.gd's sparks, debris and arc jaggedness call randf() unseeded BY DESIGN (a chain node's lightning is meant never to repeat), so two runs of byte-identical source produce different frame hashes: measured 23 differing pixels out of 1166400, one small cluster, max channel delta 279. An agent verifying a presentation-only change against a hash will therefore see a false failure and may go looking for a regression that does not exist. Future issues should specify either a pixel-diff against a repeat-run baseline of the SAME source, or a capture-time RNG seed hook. Found while verifying CAM-08.

The PostToolUse hook that parse-checks an edited .gd file (added to .claude/settings.json by PRC-01) has NOT been observed firing. Its logic was verified by feeding it real stdin JSON in Claude Code's documented shape and it behaves correctly both clean and broken, but no hook output appeared on any live Edit or Write during the session that added it -- most likely because settings.json is read once at session start, before the edit landed. Confirm in a fresh session by deliberately breaking a .gd file with Edit and checking the hook speaks up. If it does not fire, the gate's 'gdscript parses' check is the only line of defence and the hook should be removed rather than left as a comfort that does nothing.

pack_atlas.py --check cannot catch a cell-size mismatch, because 'if not write: continue' short-circuits before Image.open, so the per-image size assertion never runs in check mode. Pre-existing, but it matters now that the cell size comes from sprites.json rather than a hardcoded constant: the assertion is the only thing standing between a manifest that says 512 and renders that are 256. Make --check run the assertion.

Before ART-04 raises the atlas cell, probe GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE on this machine under GL Compatibility. pack_atlas.py's COLS=12 makes a 1024px-cell page 12288px wide; the GL spec floor is 2048 and nothing here has measured what Mesa llvmpipe and the owner's Windows GPU actually report. A page that exceeds it does not warn, it fails to upload. Flagged in a pack_atlas.py comment rather than asserted, because it is unmeasured.

tools/session.py's gate() does not forward --tier to the check.py subprocess (it forwards --no-window only). Harmless today because the default is tier 4, which is what a STATE.md regeneration wants — but a 'fast STATE regen' workflow is the obvious next ask and it would silently record a tier-1 result as though it were the full gate. If --tier is ever forwarded, the gate block STATE.md writes must also record which tier produced it.

Concurrent Godot captures do not parallelise -- they multiply. Rendering is Mesa llvmpipe software GL and one capture spreads to about 8 of this machine's 16 cores (measured: a single Godot at 788 percent CPU), so three agents capturing at once drives load average to 18.6 and turns a nine-second frame-1800 capture into minutes. Two agents then hit the 120-second command timeout and stopped mid-task waiting on it, which is how this surfaced. Consequences worth fixing: tools/shot.py should take a lease or a lock so captures serialise across agents rather than trampling each other (this is PRC-07's lease mechanism, and it is the strongest argument for it), and any multi-agent plan should treat 'launches Godot' as a scarce resource and schedule at most one or two such workstreams at a time. Measured during the theatre-scale E1 batch.

The pooled combat FX -- bolt, arc, flak, mortar and field in fx_additive.gd's main _draw() -- do not dim under brownout. Only Display.glow is applied to them, not the brownout factor that glow_layer.gd uses. CLAUDE.md is explicit that the whole reason glow is a separate additive pass is that 'brownout visibly dims every emissive element in the game' (decision 007), and the fight itself is the most emissive thing on screen. Pre-existing; surfaced while adding the sustained beam, which DOES carry the factor, so the two passes now disagree with each other. Fix is the same 0.35 multiply the beam and the glow layer already use.
check.py's module docstring says 'no .github/ directory yet' — stale since PRC-08 added .github/workflows/
items.why: tools/check.py is out of this agent's owned scope for PRC-08; docstring fix needs a session that owns that file

items.title: nightly.yml (PRC-08) runs tier 4 unsharded — wire tools/test_parity.py --shard I/N once PRC-05 lands, as a matrix job
items.why: PRC-05 had not landed when PRC-08's nightly workflow was written; the TODO is in the workflow's header comment

items.title: nightly.yml (PRC-08) reap step is report-only (no --kill) — switch to a lease-scoped tools/reap.py --kill --lease once PRC-07 lands
items.why: PRC-07's lease-scoped reap had not landed when PRC-08's nightly workflow was written; unscoped --kill on a self-hosted runner shared with the owner's own sessions would be unsafe

items.title: install the git hooks tools/install_hooks.py writes — run '.venv/bin/python tools/install_hooks.py' once no other agent has an in-flight commit/push
items.why: PRC-08's hooks were written and verified against a scratch repo but deliberately left uninstalled: seven agents were committing through this working tree concurrently and a pre-commit hook could have blocked another workstream's in-flight file

items.title: tools/check.py's three rendered checks (game renders, menu renders, accessibility) should pass an explicit --camera now that CAM-01/CAM-03 landed, so their coverage/contrast numbers stay comparable run to run instead of depending on default camera framing, which CAM-01 changed. Re-baseline after pinning. tools/check.py is owned by another workstream so this was not done as part of CAM-01/CAM-03.

scripts/test/parity.gd's _shed() reaches into AnchorSim.placed and free_slots directly rather than going through the class's own methods. One instance of this was a real bug, found by the first WAR-05 parity run: _shed() wrote s.placed[worst]['online'] = false instead of calling s.set_online(), which bypassed the per-effect list rebuild and left capacity() reading a stale restorer set -- 7 differences across anchor-23/burst at all three difficulties. Fixed for .online; the rest of the function still indexes s.placed and s.free_slots directly, so the next field that needs a hook on write reintroduces the same class of bug silently. Worth a convention note, or making the mutation points the only public way in.

pack_atlas.py can assert that a page exceeds GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE but cannot do anything about it: emitting multiple pages needs scripts/sprites.gd to resolve a sprite across pages, and it currently cannot. Measured on this machine: GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE is 16384 (Mesa llvmpipe 25.2.8, via an EGL surfaceless probe), and the asserted floor in pack_atlas.py is 4096 rather than the GLES3.0 spec minimum of 2048, because 2048 would already fail today's real 3072px page. At a 512px cell the library fits; at 1024 it will not. So multi-page resolution in sprites.gd is the actual prerequisite for ART-04 going past 512, not the assertion.

Every real render still overwrites the tracked assets/renders/_calibration.png, so even a single-asset re-render dirties a file that has nothing to do with that asset. Small residual against PRC-13's 'only what changed moves' story; pre-existing calibrate() behaviour. Either write the calibration probe to a scratch path, or stop tracking it.

Anchor-17's default camera framing (8.5,7.5,1.0) puts 2 of the anchor's 12 build slots (index 2 and 3 in free_slots order) off-screen or behind the INCOMING panel — discovered while placing towers via --build for LF-117 verification. Not a bug (players use camera pan/zoom), but worth a note in shot.py's docs so the next session doesn't re-derive which slots are visible by trial and error.

No CLI hook to force a specific pooled combat FX (bolt/arc/flak/mortar) to fire on a chosen frame — verifying LF-117's brownout dim required ~40 blind shot.py sweeps to catch a live projectile on screen, and flak/mortar were never caught firing at all despite the fix applying identically to all four classes. A --force-shot <slot> hook (or a shot_fired debug dump like ABILITY-LIVE's) would make this a two-command job.

The Bash tool's default 120-second timeout silently pushes long runs into the background rather than failing them, and agents then stop and wait -- observed four times today across four different agents (a 300-frame capture, an anchor-24 200 percent capture, a nine-minute test_parity.py, and one more). The cost is billing: a backgrounded process the harness still tracks re-invokes the model when it exits, against a session everyone believed was over. Telling an agent 'never background' is not enough, because the agent is not choosing to; the fix is to tell it to pass an explicit timeout up to 600000ms on any command that could exceed two minutes, and to say WHICH commands those are. Candidates for a documented list in CLAUDE.md: test_parity.py (~9 min), check.py tier 3 and 4, sim/run.py and sweep.py without --jobs, any shot.py capture while the machine is loaded (LF-116), and a full Blender library render (~2m12s).

Capped-core policies structurally exclude support towers from the closed candidate set, which confounds every escort-value claim on an anchor carrying air units. Concrete case, measured: lance-core (2 ion-lance + pulse-turret fill) LOSES anchor-13 at all three difficulties -- 13 leaks, 0 lives by wave 8 -- while burst (open, unlimited lance) wins all three. The cause is not the escort: neither ion-lance nor pulse-turret has reveal, so a closed policy cannot target reach-skiff or warden-mote at all, a cost burst never pays because scan-relay stays available to it. So the anchor-13 escort claim reads as refuted when what was actually tested was 'no reveal at all'. Needs a policy shape that keeps one designated support tower available outside the core/fill accounting, or the escort question stays unfalsifiable for exactly the anchors it matters on.

mortar-core (2 mortar-emplacement + flak-array fill) is a strictly better board than anything the original twelve policies ever found, and BAL-04 needs to know before it re-tunes anything. It wins anchor-13 at all three difficulties where anti-armour loses hard and brutal, and contributes 29 new distinct winning compositions across 12 anchors -- flak+mortar on 09, 12, 13, 16, 17, 19, 20, 21, 23, 24, plus lance+turret on 14 and 15. Every published pass/fail cell is unchanged, so nothing regressed; what changed is that several Act II and III anchors now have an intended solution the grader had never been able to express. Re-read those anchors' design intent against it.

PRESSURE_FLOOR is confirmed dead a second way and now needs an owner decision rather than another measurement. LF-054 found peak load at or above capacity in every anchor-by-difficulty cell. Re-measured under the four new capped-core policies, and additionally restricted to WINNING builds only -- the alternative LF-054 itself proposed -- it is still 0 of 72 cells failing. So the check cannot discriminate under any policy set the grader can currently express. Either raise the floor to a value that does discriminate, or delete it and stop implying the grader tests something it does not.

sim/content.py's all_anchor_ids() discovers anchors with a raw glob('anchor-*.json') over data/anchors/, so ANY untracked file dropped there is treated as real content. Measured consequence: a scratch 64x64 synthetic anchor used for a draw-path benchmark was picked up by tools/density.py and broke the gate's wave density check outright -- act 1 suddenly had a 700-unit anchor as its busiest reference. validate_data.py is already immune because PRC-02 moved it to git ls-files; content.py was not converted because nothing pointed at it. Same reasoning applies: a scratch or generated anchor is not content until it is tracked. This will bite again the moment anyone builds the large-board generator (TS-05/LF-080), which is exactly a workflow of generate, grade, discard.

CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is per top-level CLI session, NOT per subagent, so the reaper's new own-session lease class is coarser than 'this agent'. Discovered while building the leases: reap.py --json showed a live test_parity.py and a batch of godot --check-only processes carrying the SAME session id as the agent inspecting them, because a sibling subagent fanned out by the same orchestrator inherits it -- which is exactly the fan-out pattern CLAUDE.md prescribes. Consequence: plain reap.py --kill can still silently end a live sibling subagent's process. It is narrower than the old kill-by-command-shape behaviour but it is not safe, and the remaining hole is precisely the multi-agent case the leases were built for. No finer identifier is exposed in the environment; tightening own-session to never auto-kill would break the leftover-cleanup path SessionEnd depends on. Needs either a harness-exposed per-subagent id or a design change -- until then the honest rule is that only --all is ever safe to reason about, and plain --kill is safe only in a single-agent session.

tools/test_parity.py's run_godot() has no timeout on its own subprocess.run, so a wedged Godot hangs the parity run itself indefinitely. The new lease TTL bounds when ANOTHER session may reap that process, which is a different problem -- it does nothing for the run that is stuck waiting on it. Parity is the longest thing in the gate at 9m40s and 1152 runs, so a hang there is also the most expensive one to sit through. Every other gate subprocess is already bounded (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT 300s, PARITY_TIMEOUT 1800s in check.py); this is the one that got missed because it bounds itself from the outside.

MAX_CONCURRENT_CAPTURES=2 in tools/lease.py is unit-tested but never live-validated. The bound comes from a real measurement -- one Godot capture takes about 8 of this machine's 16 cores, and three concurrent captures drove load average to 18.6 and turned a nine-second frame into minutes (LF-116) -- but the cap itself was only exercised against three threads and a fake workload, not against real concurrent shot.py and gate captures, because doing that safely needs a window when no other agent is working in the tree. Validate it then, and record whether 2 is actually the right number or whether the honest answer is 1.

anchor-09's new flank lane (WAR-01's acceptance case) is unwinnable at hard and brutal and needs a sweep before it is real content. Measured, before vs after adding the second lane: standard 11 of 16 winning builds becomes 2 of 16, hard 9 becomes 0, brutal 6 becomes 0. Peak load barely moved (162 to 139 percent standard), so this is not a power problem -- it is that a second entrance splits coverage on a board whose slots were placed for one. That is exactly the design pressure multi-lane is supposed to create, so the fix is a tuning pass on spawn counts or slot placement, not backing the lane out. It was landed deliberately light to prove the plumbing rather than to be balanced.

tools/analysis_lf014.py carries a hardcoded /Users/briangerhards/dev/defend-claude sys.path from a different machine, so it cannot run here at all. It was mechanically updated for the multi-lane point_at signature but that edit is UNVERIFIED BY EXECUTION -- nothing in the gate runs this file, and its syntax passing is the only thing anyone knows about it. Either fix the path and give it a smoke run, or delete it: an analysis script nobody can execute is a claim with no evidence behind it, which is the opposite of what this repo's tooling is for.

The HUD threat panel and the dialog both still say 'the lane', singular, now that an anchor can carry up to five. Deferred deliberately by WAR-01 rather than missed. Control reads the bus figure aloud in every brief and tools/say_capacity.py reconciles that, so there is precedent for prose that has to track data -- but lane count is harder, because 'hold the lane' is a line of characterisation, not a number to substitute. Needs a narrative pass over the affected briefs once more than one anchor is genuinely multi-lane, not a find-and-replace.

`--press-at` in main.gd dispatches straight to AnchorView._action_input(), bypassing the real input pipeline — an lf_* action handled in a different node's _unhandled_input (e.g. hud.gd's lf_hud_toggle) is invisible to it. Verifying such actions needs a per-feature CLI hook (see hud.gd's --hud-hidden) rather than --press-at.

Disabled SELL/UPGRADE button text (C_DIM on C_PANEL, 'SELL —' / 'UPGRADE —') measures 4.6-4.7:1 — passes AA but fails the AAA/7:1 bar the rest of the type ladder was solved for (decisions 045/046). a11y.py flags it as a warning on every HUD capture.

Wire a gate check for YAW_HYSTERESIS_FRAC < 0.5 into tools/check.py. The constant is now a FRACTION of a bucket rather than a bare degree count, which is what makes it survive a change to YAW_COUNT -- but a fraction at or above 0.5 exceeds half a bucket and freezes every emplacement's facing permanently, which is exactly the LF-108 failure the fraction was introduced to prevent. sprites.gd asserts it at boot, so the game catches it; the gate does not. About five lines: read scripts/iso.gd, extract the constant, assert it is under 0.5. Was not added with ART-02 because check.py belonged to another workstream that hour.

tools/yaw_band.py and scripts/test/facing.gd read anchor_sim.gd's wave_queue() and spawn() shapes directly, so they break silently whenever those change -- and one such break was hit and fixed during the same session that introduced them, when the multi-lane migration changed wave_queue() to emit [time, lane, enemy_id]. Neither file is run by any gate tier, so the next drift will be discovered by whoever next needs a facing measurement, mid-task, exactly as it was this time. Either give them a cheap smoke check in the gate or make them consume a shared accessor rather than the tuple layout.

Multi-lane camera framing: on anchor-09 the flank lane's exit sits outside the default-zoom frame, because _default_target() can pan but not zoom to fit, and two exits on opposite edges of a 16x13 board cannot both be in frame at one zoom. Presentation only and pre-existing in shape -- decision 056 accepted detail loss at zoom-out, and CAM-01 derives a minimum zoom that fits the board, so the material is all there. What is missing is that the opening framing does not USE it: a multi-lane anchor should open at whatever zoom shows every spawn and every exit, not at 1.0 centred on lane 0. Becomes more visible with every lane added.

sfx determinism failed once for a subagent mid-session and passed on every other run, including twice immediately afterwards on the same tree ('ui_confirm byte-identical'). The agent attributed it to pre-existing audio synthesis nondeterminism; nothing supports that and the check has been green every other time it has run today. More likely a transient under heavy concurrent load, or a partially-written file read by a check racing whatever produced it. Filed so the next occurrence is a second data point rather than a first one -- if it recurs, capture both WAVs and diff them rather than trusting either explanation.
